text:
Maya Li: Heads up — BigBank legal just asked for an emergency routing exemption. They want requests with header `X-Org-Route: bigbank-dedicated` to always go to their dedicated pool, bypassing normal cost-based routing. They claim latency SLOs are contractual.

Sam O'Connor: uh, do we have precedent for header-based forced routing?

Maya Li: Not exactly. We have per-tenant mappings in the routing DB, and we have header-based hints for experimental routing. This would be an enforced override — no fallback to cheaper models.

Jordan: Are they talking about all endpoints (chat/embedding/generate) or just generate?

Maya Li: All inference requests. They want routing done before model selection and before batching/caching layers so they never hit shared fleets.

KT: Security/cost concern: anyone who can set that header could force expensive capacity unless we gate it. Must be tied to org-level allowlist + token validation.

Sam O'Connor: +1. We should require (a) API key binding in our auth system to mark org as allowed-for-header-override, and (b) console toggle per-org that grants the permit.

Jordan: Also add audit trail and telemetry flags so billing/alerts show override usage. Suggest label `routing.override=org_forced` and `routing.source=header` in traces.

Maya Li: Agreed. BigBank also wants a console checkbox that says "Force dedicated routing". Legal wants measurable meters for SLA.

KT: Implementation notes: Routing precedence must be unambiguous. Proposed order: `explicit per-org mapping (highest) -> header override if org is allowlisted -> policy fallback (cost/latency) -> global default`. If we put header override above per-org mapping, we risk breaking pinned mappings.

Sam O'Connor: That ordering sounds right. Also need a kill-switch: org-level emergency toggle that ops can flip to remove override if capacity issues happen.

Ops QA: Would be great to have automatic throttling/backpressure to the dedicated pool if their requests exceed capacity, with a configured SLA breach path. We can't let one org starve others.

Maya Li: Right — contractually they get certain throughput, but we should implement burst protection and circuit-breaker with backpressure policy that notifies account team and triggers fallback only if permitted by contract.

Jordan: Quick draft rule snippet for router (pseudo):
```
- match: header `X-Org-Route` == "bigbank-dedicated"
  condition: org_allowlist.contains(org_id) && api_key.bound_to_org == org_id
  action: route_to: dedicated/bigbank-pool
  telemetry: add_tags ["routing.override","routing.source:header"]
  audit: emit event routing.override.request
```

KT: We also need console UX copy — must make it explicit that enabling forces traffic to dedicated infra and may incur extra charges. And require two-person confirmation for enablement? maybe okay to start with owner+billing consent flow.

Sam O'Connor: Ops workflows: ensure canary deploys still work. If a model rollout changes kernel selection on the dedicated pool, BigBank can't be silently affected. We need per-pool rollout controls.

Maya Li: Action items: 1) Product: design console toggle + consent flow. 2) Auth: extend api-key metadata + allowlist check. 3) Router: implement header-gated rule, precedence and audit hooks. 4) Observability: tagging and dashboard for override traffic. 5) Ops: emergency kill-switch + capacity guard.

KT: I'll open a small RFC and include the pseudo-rule + failure modes.

devops-bot: config-deploy/staging started for routing-rule branch `feat/bigbank-header-override` — CI passed, deploying to staging. :rocket:

Ops QA: I'll run load test against staging with header set and verify batching, KV cache behavior, and billing tags.

Sam O'Connor: One more security thought: strip `X-Org-Route` on entry unless token proves org owner. Don't allow user-supplied header from client unless proxied by our gateway after auth.

Maya Li: Good call. We'll only honor header after gateway enrichment step.

Jordan: I'll add telemetry dashboards: per-org override usage, latency differential vs normal routing, and SLO alerts when override traffic exceeds threshold.

Maya Li: Thanks team. I'll sync with BigBank AM and legal, update contract language for the kill-switch and telemetry SLA.

Sam O'Connor: Great. Keep thread updated with RFC link. :thumbsup:
